We had eight entrants; and our sympathy went out to Bert Field, who, after a three months' conscientious preparation, had the misfortune to sustain a slight foot injury on the eve of the race and had to content himself as a spectator from the bus-top.
Arthur Penny recorded fastest time and we expect him to be very prominent over the country this year. Bert Field was another to show improvement in taking second place in the Walk Handicap, and H.
Bert Field, despite a pull for second prize in the preceding Club handicap, took the third handicap prize.
Bert Field walked the race of his life, and Alf. Harley fought the Surrey boys in a style that thoroughly earned a place in the winning team.

The day was a fine one, and at the start Fred Rickards, Tommy Green and Bert Field set up a brisk start. Saunders, who is usually a slow starter but a most strong and resolute finisher, surprised in this race by being right up with the leaders for several miles.
The evening's programme had begun with a walk which was well won by Bert Field, fresh from an excellent 20 miles performance four days previously, in fast time.
For us, full marks go to Bert Field, who, despite a gruelling thirty-odd miles two days before, pluckily turned out at short notice and did very well to finish 8th.
Bert Field was as dependable as ever, and with a litle good fortune and more experience, will soon be having a say in the destination of the individual championships.
Our sealed handicap held in conjunction provided our Walking Hon. Secretary with a "First," with Bert Field second, and L. Jones, continuing in his great promise, third.

Joe King was second man home, and with Bert Field completing the team, we were placed second in the scratch team race. Both scratch and team events went to the Surrey Walking Club, who had a very fine day out, for in addition they supplied first (H.

Fifth position was filled by Bert Field, his usual consistent self, which makes him such a reliable team man. Harley, who finished sixth, fell away slightly over the last three miles, but was nearly six minutes faster than last year; R.

Bert Field completed our team a place behind Martin, and once again illustrated his extreme dependability. Our four scored 42 points, but Surrey Walking Club, the holders, had managed to retain their title by scoring 40 points.

Immediately following our third man, Green, were "Jock" Martin and Bert Field, giving the finest support to our scoring team that it would be possible to have.

Our team this year contained only three of the eight who did duty for us last year, the absentees being such well-known walkers as Tommy Green, Fred Rickards, Jack Bidgood, Bert Field and Bill Holman.
Our next were walking in trio, Bentley 13th, Rickards 14th, Bidgood 15th, and still the team chances looked rosy. Joe King had dropped a bit, Bert Field was 32nd and Alf 34th, but alas!
Our heartiest congratulations and very best wishes go to Joe Coleman, Bert Field and Jim Ginty upon their respective marriages. We wish them all years of health and happiness.
